notes.title: Devlog #13: The Sand Mask: A Source of Inspiration – May 28th, 2025
notes.content:
Hi, Gamers! 

Tina here—Social Media Expert and Host at RolldBox Games. Today, I’m chatting with Cris, the Art Director of the studio at RolldBox Games and Ferran, one of our Co-Founders, as well as the Game Designer and Creative Director of the studio at RolldBox Games 👋 


We’re getting closer and closer to the moment we can finally share Masks of the Void with all of you — it’s not far off now!

We can’t wait for you to discover the story behind this anti-stress roguelite, as some of our playtesters call it.

While the launch approaches, we wanted to give you another glimpse into how we get inspired and how we bring our ideas to life.

We know you love seeing how the team works behind the scenes — so here’s a brand-new Devlog just for you!


Inside the Development Process

We shared some details about the Sand Mask in our last Devlog, and now we want to take you deeper into how we came up with it:

From both the Art and Game Design sides, our goal with all the masks is to convey strength, power, and intensity. That feeling comes through in the shape of each mask, its powers, and the effects crafted by our Technical Artist to bring everything to life. 

For the Sand Mask, in particular, the Game Design team focused on a single-direction launch mechanic. We wanted it to channel the Glass Cannon archetype — and what better material than sand to hint at something as fragile and sharp as glass? ✨

🔹 We designed this mask to let you take down powerful enemies like the Sand Guards in a single hit — but only if your spatial awareness is on point:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/4824e194c065e948e6b7e63b105b8ff3301cb785.gif

And to match all that power, we had to find the tricky balance in Iret’s cloak effects: showing the maximum info in the simplest way possible, with style and clarity.

🔹 What do you think of this Sand Mask cloak? Once again, we want the mask’s power to stand out in this World of Sand:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/69e2d5611ee95160b4d3ee19ba7389d41ec5b3a5.png

Sneak Peek of Upcoming Content

Speaking of masks, let’s check out what the Blood Mask can do — and you can try it yourself in the available Demo.

Did you know you can grab every object around you, make them orbit, and throw them whenever you want?

Give it a try and share your thoughts!

🔹 We're showing off this awesome poster our Art Team made — again, because it just looks too cool not to!
What do you think?


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/f010070bbc4d49c8fdb5c408a5cc2b0b46d2b67c.png


More to share

Don’t forget to try the Infinite Waves mode in the demo — still live on our Steam page!

Get some training in and get ready to enjoy the full game soon!


See you in the next Devlog with more and better!

Don’t forget to join our Discord server! Let us know what you’d like us to talk about next from there!


See you in the Void!

notes.title: Devlog #12: Secrets of the Sand – May 13th, 2025
notes.content:
Hi, Gamers! 

Tina here—Social Media Expert and Host at RolldBox Games. Today, I’m chatting with Cris, the Art Director of the studio at RolldBox Games 👋


We love sharing and breaking down how we created Masks of the Void for you!

This fast-paced roguelite is all about power—different abilities you’ll unlock, and the real challenge: how far are you willing to push them?

We can’t wait for you to experience the full version soon!
In the meantime, we’ll keep dropping more behind-the-scenes details 😉


Inside the Development Process

We’ve been talking about enemies for a while, and in our latest devlog we introduced Ranged—one of the Sand Guards you’ll have to face.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/5f2a174202f19929cb7becc2ccff0c37afdab070.gif

These creatures were created by the Tyrant to defend and protect its domain.

You’ve already seen a few types… but trust us, there’s more to come.


Today we’re showcasing some very special ones—emerging straight from the sand: the Elemental Sand Guards.

At first glance, they might look fragile, like they could vanish in a flash…

Are you sure about that?

Jump into the action and see how fast they move—then let us know if dodging them was really that easy.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/3ac340a0140de81536cd75f7185c3ba0e2921ab3.png

And we can’t forget about our beloved Chasers!

Find out when they show up and what they do while you’re playing—then tell us what kind of impact these desert creatures had on you.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/a9d53c12a55895aeb4449497689c8390fcc83cd0.png


Sneak Peek of Upcoming Content


In the Sand world, it’s time to learn a bit more about the Sand Mask.

With it, you can levitate all nearby objects and, after 1 second, launch them at your target.

These objects might break on impact—causing a blast of debris all around.

🔹 Check out this awesome poster our Art Team made to make it shine!

What do you think?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/52004e3aec37d50b6c02b3e593b2c76368ca7942.png


More to share

Speaking of masks—don’t forget the Blood Mask is also available in the demo, and you can try it out right now!

We’ll be sharing more about it in our next post.



See you in the next Devlog with more and better!

Don’t forget to join our Discord server! Let us know what you’d like us to talk about next from there!

notes.title: Devlog #11: The Tyrant’s Architects – April 29th, 2025
notes.content:
Hi, Gamers! 

Tina here—Social Media Expert and Host at RolldBox Games. Today, I’m chatting with Cris, the Art Director of the studio at RolldBox Games 👋


We’re all set — Masks of the Void is just about ready for you to experience in its full version, and we want to show you what the enemy hordes are like. This roguelite was built for you, and trust us — you’re going to want to see what’s coming.

Ready to face them?


Inside the Development Process

In our last Devlog #10, we gave you a sneak peek at Melee, one of the Sand Guards you'll encounter in the Vortex world. But he’s not the only enforcer the Tyrant has created to protect his domain.

We’ve got more defenders of the Vortex — more "enemies" for you to face, like the Dasher.
These creatures will charge towards the player with a dash and deal damage on impact. They’ll stay alive until you take them down or stun them.


The type of impact will depend on when Iret interacts with the Dasher.
Defining, creating, and animating them — it’s no easy feat to make sure they pack the punch we’re going for! 🔥

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/922a88eea7554fe7c9a148457dacddb3baaca2ba.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/c54fb2d597477df1d9355f763c37f6e6b84b2a6d.gif

How many more enemies will Iret face? How many more enforcers has the Tyrant created to protect himself?

When you dive deeper into the story, you’ll uncover much more about the Tyrant and his origins. But for now, the consequences of his actions are what you’ll see!

Another Sand Guard you’ll encounter is the Ranged — he’ll stare you down before launching an attack.

Can you neutralize him?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/f72a849350250fe3256a2c5c40f7dc84bea1fd2d.png

More to share

We hope that, sooner rather than later, you’ll get to experience the full story of Masks of the Void in all its glory — we can’t wait for you to dive in and enjoy it.

Every corner and space where Iret will need to use the power of the masks!

In the meantime, we encourage you to make the most of the Vortex area you’re exploring in the Demo.

notes.title: Devlog #9: Iret Uncovered– April 1st, 2025
notes.content:
Hi, Gamers! 

Tina here—Social Media Expert and Host at RolldBox Games. Today, I’m chatting with Cris, the Art Director of the studio at RolldBox Games 👋

We love crafting these experiences with you in mind, aiming to make them as immersive as possible. Today, we’re diving deeper into the details behind our refined art. There are so many layers—literally! Here’s more about our protagonist, Iret, in this DevLog.

Inside the Development Process

As mentioned in Devlog #8, Iret’s layers were meticulously designed to deliver the smooth, dynamic movement we envisioned. We defined and added plenty of bones to maximize flexibility and adaptability. You can see the result in this side-scrolling scene of Iret.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/10c1437372dee1d8728b3832aa616bd8cc46b48b.gif

On top of that, our Technical Artist has taken the layer effects to the next level. We didn’t stop until every linked mask projected its corresponding effect onto the layer—crisp, powerful, and crystal clear.

What was the biggest challenge? Translating the concept art—with the exact color palette for each mask and outfit—into a final in-game effect that looks just right. This meant considering the camera’s perspective, the chaos of combat, and the overall game flow.

🔹 Here’s the Concept Art:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/69e2d5611ee95160b4d3ee19ba7389d41ec5b3a5.png

🔹 Here’s the layer effect with the Sand Mask:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/992af63b56a00aae9aefc8098b9160b959c5f4a3.gif

🔹 And here’s the layer effect with the Blood Mask:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/4c1a8a5ac32282aef89a972a7c610f99fb503913.gif

Sneak Peek of Upcoming Content

Let’s talk about Iret’s interactions with NPCs, bosses, and enemies. Guess how many AIs we’ve set up? Over 50 unique configurations to ensure a diverse gameplay experience!

In the meantime, here’s something cool: the first AIs we created were the Soldier and Dasher, which you can check out in the image:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/73ff297eaa201116ffa5b133f3452509e8c81217.gif

More to share

Remember how to unlock the second Mask in the Demo?

At the end of the demo, once you've completed that section of the game, you can unlock the second mask – the ‘Blood’ Mask. Have you figured out how it works yet?

Each mask unlocks a new way to use telekinesis.

Which one do you think is the most fun to use?



See you in the next Devlog with more and better!

Don’t forget to join our Discord server! Let us know what you’d like us to talk about next from there!

notes.title: Devlog #8: Art From the Inside – March 18th, 2025
notes.content:
Hi, Gamers! 

Tina here—Social Media Expert and Host at RolldBox Games. Today, I’m chatting with Cris, the Art Director of the studio at RolldBox Games 👋

The art in a video game is insanely complex, and we have to consider many aspects to make sure it hits the mark on the story we want to tell, the game feeling we want to create, and that it fully matches the intended gameplay. Today, we’re pulling back the curtain to give you a closer look at the details!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/65e3ff9d44ab430c3cf3120a94edd531912ed7ee.gif

Inside the Development Process

As we mentioned in Devlog #7, we covered the throwable objects. Today, we’re diving into how we make them both “breakable” and “throwable”:

To give all throwable objects a realistic feel, placing their pivot point at the center of mass is crucial, considering their shape to figure out where the weight naturally balances. Blender came in clutch here, as it has a built-in feature to set the pivot point at the center of mass.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/0ebe52bd4155dfae3e01985a891d3c284cdcb6c1.png

For breakable and throwable props, making sure the pivot is as centered as possible was essential. While using Unreal’s destruction system, the generated pieces would keep their pivot in the center. But not all objects used Unreal’s system—we crafted the pieces by hand, like bones, to make sure the way they broke into parts made sense.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/18685cefd71f10b7e7bfb1c1e8db7f04fecf8399.png

Sneak Peek of Upcoming Content

Iret's capes, the design, creation, and animation process, have evolved several times. Here’s how we animated them:

We’re all about showing that they have a lot of bones because we want their movement to be superfluid, and that meant animating the capes by hand for each animation, which took a lot of time. To optimize it, we decided to use Unreal’s physics system for most animations, allowing them to move more organically with Iret’s body. For some specific animations, like the basic and special attacks with the different masks, where we needed the capes to have more complex movements, we spent extra time hand-animating them to get the exact movement we wanted.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/5be9f07c106d8d374066ec54ea1c5ccf3ee11f31.gif


More to share

Don’t forget to dive into the story or the Infinite Waves and discover the different types of relics!
Want to know the secret to survive longer? Grab and combine relics of the same theme to unlock powerful synergies! ⚙️

Think you’re ready to take it on?


See you in the next Devlog with more and better!

Don’t forget to join our Discord server! Let us know what you’d like us to talk about next from there!


See you in the Void!

notes.title: Devlog #7: How Our Physics Work – March, 5th 2025
notes.content:
Hi, Gamers! 

Tina here—Social Media Expert and Host at RolldBox Games. Today, I’m chatting with Ferran, one of our Co-Founders, as well as the Game Designer and Creative Director of the studio at RolldBox Games 👋

The #SteamNextFest just wrapped up, where our demo was available, and we're super excited that you enjoyed it! Thanks for participating!

Just a reminder, the free demo is still up, and you can dive into what we're talking about today — the physics in our game, based on telekinesis and the ability to throw everything around you.



Inside the Development Process

In the early versions of the game, we were working in Unreal 4 without access to the Fracture Mode. This feature completely changed our performance and how we handled object breaking, making it more realistic.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/cf24aa0fa1b7df225fc0eea9b6b8ed8060540f3a.gif

That being said, we've used Unreal Engine's native physics system, making sure to implement CCD, a collision checker that's a must when dealing with high-speed objects.

In some cases, certain AI entities need collision response settings for throwables, depending on whether we want them to respond with their typical capsule or their mesh, like with the Void creatures.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/b3a65ec86d862173390e985e5cb0e2693f37a168.gif

Sneak Peek of Upcoming Content

The art team has been crucial in shaping, creating, and designing all the objects you can find in Masks of the Void, which you can throw and break. In each zone, in every part of the game, you'll find various elements—different shapes, textures, and colors—all specifically crafted.

Here’s a sneak peek at some of these objects!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/f89d17462be9aa83ca4cd28425bc898de6c8d773.png


More to share

Do you know what the dev team's favorite mask is? Well, we’ve got a tie between the different ones! In the demo, you can try out the Sand and Blood masks.

Which one’s your favorite? Share your opinion and have fun with them! And don’t forget to play Infinite Waves and join the Leaderboard. 🏆



See you in the next Devlog with more and better!

Don’t forget to join our Discord server! Let us know what you’d like us to talk about next from there!


See you in the Void!

notes.title: Devlog #6: Unique Dev Challenges – February 19th, 2025
notes.content:
Hi, Gamers! 

Tina here—Social Media Expert and Host at RolldBox Games. Today, I’m chatting with Ferran, one of our Co-Founders, as well as the Game Designer and Creative Director of the studio at RolldBox Games 👋

We're making steady progress on the final product, and today, we're excited to share some behind-the-scenes programming insights. There’s a lot that goes into development, so we’ve picked two key aspects to give you a glimpse of what’s happening under the hood. Writing scalable code, harnessing Unreal’s full power, and ensuring top-notch performance are always at the core of our process.

Let’s dive in!


Inside the Development Process

In the relic system, one of the biggest challenges has been designing subsystems in advance to keep relic families (those with shared behaviors) scalable. This way, we can implement new relics and synergies without having to rework older ones every time we add something fresh. Plus, we've made sure all these modifiers seamlessly integrate with the game's core systems—physics, object manipulation, abilities, enemies, and more.

There’s a solid lineup of relics in the full game (you’ll see for yourself!), all crafted just for you. 🔮 


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/b5a69237ee82f5f1d0972c6bc7f92da9d2bfb943.gif

Sneak Peek of Upcoming Content

This game revolves around telekinesis and the ability to move objects, making physics management a top priority. You can move everything around you... except for the ground!

Unreal Engine’s physics have a solid core, but they’re packed with tiny details that shape how the gameplay feels—especially in the middle of all the chaos. Fine-tuning how Unreal handles all the math and nailing that satisfying "throwing stuff" experience has been a challenge from day one.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/f5237cc8a16e51cfdda98ea306a57d28bad4c703.gif


More to share

Enjoy the demo in Story Mode too!

Today, we’re sharing which relic we, as a team, found the easiest to use in the demo: the Base Shots with effects. They’re super simple—just apply fire, poison, or bleed, for example. 

Make the most of them in Infinite Waves and climb the Leaderboard while you're at it!



See you in the next Devlog with more and better!

Don’t forget to join our Discord server! Let us know what you’d like us to talk about next from there!


See you in the Void!

notes.title: Devlog #5: Performance Matters – February 5th, 2025
notes.content:
Hi, Gamers! 

Tina here—Social Media Expert and Host at RolldBox Games. Today, I’m chatting with Cris,  Art Director of the studio at RolldBox Games 👋

We're deep into the development, and we can't wait for you to experience the Full version soon!

We love sharing insights into the different aspects of game development—just like we’ve been doing with these Devlogs…

As many have said before, making a video game is no easy feat—especially when striving for cohesion and consistency across all elements to craft the best possible experience for you. That’s the spirit driving us every step of the way.


Inside the Development Process

Today, we want to dive into the challenges of optimizing game performance. Besides the tricks we've shown you, there's a lot more to uncover.

Balancing artistic vision with technical constraints is key to finding the sweet spot between visual quality and performance. To achieve this, we’ve used a variety of techniques throughout development—from reusing assets with variations to strategically crafting scene composition and camera angles, among others.

Scene set in the Market zone:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/4bcf165cae9954c7b16cdf7a4e8ed1f79014ffbc.png

Scene with no post-processing or lighting adjustments:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/09d89b1f332055e01578bbd3ba6d352cc076776e.png


Sneak Peek of Upcoming Content

We can't overlook the number of throwables in this game, where the ability to move objects—telekinesis—plays a major role!

Here's an example for you, and you'll get a sneak peek at the kinds of actions you can pull off! 🙂 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/541e8e62d19b83f85f546206302968752c252599.png

The game's overlap system and all the physics involved have been an ongoing challenge: the sheer number of interactions happening at once, keeping characters from flying off after an impact, for instance. And when you throw in the relics and all their possibilities, you can't even imagine how many collateral effects we have to account for!


More to share

…and, don’t forget to dive into Infinite Waves and climb the Leaderboard.

Want to know one of the secrets to lasting longer? Grab and combine relics of the same theme. You’ll discover the synergies they create!

Ready to take it on?

notes.title: Devlog #4: Art Development Challenges – January 22nd, 2025
notes.content:
Hi, Gamers! 

Tina here—Social Media Expert and Host at RolldBox Games. Today, I’m chatting with Cris,  Art Director of the studio at RolldBox Games 👋

We’ve kicked off 2025 with tons of energy and are working hard to wrap up the full development of Masks of the Void so you can dive in as soon as possible!

Today, we're sharing more details about the game and what we’re up to. Hope you enjoy it!


Inside the Development Process

In the full version of the game, you’ll get to fully explore the world of the Void. 

One of the key aspects we’ve focused on is the architecture of this world. So, where did the real challenge lie? It was all about nailing the right balance—figuring out the perfect number of pieces and their variety to bring the Void we envisioned to life. You know what they say, “easier said than done”, and turning our ideas into an efficient, playable design that delivers a great experience with the right performance is always a tough quest.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/42cde3f4791a195cfc579a6eb400265dcd6c58ff.png

Sneak Peek of Upcoming Content

Game performance always tests us when it comes to striking the tricky balance between delivering a visually captivating experience and ensuring smooth gameplay. Our art team uses various techniques to optimize visual resources. One example is a fake fog material we use in several areas. Its versatility and logic have been applied to other elements as well, like the sand dunes found in the Vortex.

notes.title: Devlog #2: Some Insights into the Void Development – December 30th, 2024
notes.content:
Hi, Gamers!

Tina here—Social Media Expert and Host at RolldBox Games. Today, I’m chatting with Cris, the Art Director at RolldBox Games 👋

As we wrap up 2024, we’re looking back at the tons of work we've put into Masks of the Void, and we hope you’re having a blast with what you can try out in the DEMO.
Let me give you the lowdown on some of the stuff we’re prepping for you with the team!


Inside the Development Process

In the world of the Void, there’s a lot to discover, and in this case, we’re sharing a moment from the cinematic created by our art team, where you'll meet all the followers of the Neverending Night.

Making a short, engaging, and super intuitive cinematic is one of our constant challenges to connect with you in a dynamic way, making sure the experience flows and aligns perfectly with the game’s pace.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/08fb6dc2c9e998cab04021a8c92fb6fa12dfb994.gif

Sneak Peek of Upcoming Content

How do you imagine the Void? Today, we’re talking about one of the creatures you'll encounter in the Void!

Do you have enough skill to take it on? Here’s a sneak peek as it’s gearing up for one of its attacks, featuring one of the many VFX effects our Technical Artist has crafted with serious attention to detail.

More to share

And don’t forget to play Infinite Waves and join the Leaderboard.

In the first few days, the participation was instant, and check out the scores that were posted early on, in the first 48 hours!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/da4424f5df14c165eede1f27b21b0c55f5f3d71f.png

The ranking has probably shifted a lot, and we have no idea where you stand!
Have you dared to give it a try?


See you in the next Devlog with more and better!

Don’t forget to join our Discord server! Let us know what you’d like us to talk about next from there!


See you in the Void!

notes.title: Devlog #1: What we do with Masks of the Void – December 20th, 2024
notes.content:
Hi, Gamers!

Tina here—Social Media Expert and Host at RolldBox Games. Today, I’m chatting with Ferran, one of our Co-Founders, as well as the Game Designer and Creative Director of the studio. 👋

After working on this project for a long time and with the release of the DEMO, we’re excited to share what’s being done to bring the development process to completion. We’ll keep sharing tidbits with you so you can get a sneak peek behind the scenes. Let’s get started!
That’s why we’re thrilled to share insights into the production of Masks of the Void, from the unique perspectives of our team members.

Inside the Development Process

As we progress in the development of Masks of the Void, we’ve been working on several features and want to create a space for you to catch a glimpse of what’s in the works and how it’s evolving.
One thing we were excited to share, for example, is the evolution of the UI and how it has changed over time through playtesting. Among all the UI elements, the upgrades screen stands out—the one that allows IRET to develop its power during a run. This UI has undergone several changes, as we’ve been simplifying and refining it over time, such as:

1st Iteration

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/0f7eb9df109dced6019bb3c7db7060e863551b84.png

2nd iteration

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/b359690607ae52b40edadeb7b9d311001eedfe40.png

And now it looks like:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/92aa3684c1ee950d2eeaebb3744ade52dc401924.png

Developing this UI was a massive effort, trying to balance letting the player know what can be done without overwhelming them with too many buttons. We ended up placing all the options on the same screen, with an unbalanced distribution, to let players know they can develop IRET and also perform some secondary actions with the Energy.



Sneak Peek of Upcoming Content

In every Devlog, we will be showing some of the upcoming details of the game as part of the full development of Masks of the Void. For today’s opening blog, we are delighted to share what the Void realm looks like! Have you ever wondered where the Cultists come from?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45342879/c3e61b83f2b2340ad1d8df7529667e906c4a1ebb.png

More to share

In the demo, you can already practice with two masks! 

Reach the end of the story, and you’ll unlock a second one: the Blood mask, where you’ll discover new forms of telekinesis. Give it a try and let us know what you think!

See you in the next Devlog with more and better!

Don’t forget to join our Discord server! Let us know what you’d like us to talk about next from there!

See you in the Void!
